items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 NaturalSpawner.spawnCategoryForChunk computes top = getHeight(WORLD_SURFACE) + 1 and samples y = randomBetweenInclusive(minY, top), i.e. [minY, H+1]. systemic_note: One systemic thread dominates 26.1.1's Batch 3: the 26.1.1 tree did NOT inherit the 26.1 tree's behaviour fixes - it carries 26.2/26.3-form behaviour the 26.1 tree deliberately removed (same pattern Batch 2 reported for level/ behaviour, Batch 1 for fluids), contradicting PORT-NOTES-26.1.1.md's carry-forward claim. The regressions cluster exactly where 26.1's form differs from 26.2/26.3: tag-grounded behaviour for tags 26.1.1 lacks (G03, G14, G15, G32, G36, G44), component-form behaviour for components 26.1.1 data lacks (G33), 26.2-form tables (G30, G31, G46), moved gates (G29), and dropped 26.1-only code paths (G13, G35, G37, G38, G40, G41, G42, G43, G45). All 15 of 26.1's Batch 3 defects reproduce, four 1.21.7 items 26.1 had cleared regress (G03, G13, G14, G15), and 18 new defects (G29-G46) were found - the 26.1.1 tree is further from vanilla than the 26.1 tree on every axis this batch measures. The sharpest instances are the two majors: B3-G22 (the #causes_suffocation tag gate, a startup blocker; #suppresses_bounce fails first) and B3-G14 (endermen never teleport). Two of the 26.1 tree's 'corrections' were themselves wrong (mob-looting persistence, spawn-egg peaceful gate) - the 26.1.1 tree is right on those two by accident of carrying the 26.2 form. The oracle groups are the same thread on the test side, unchanged from 26.1: all 52 failing oracles reference 26.3-only APIs (EntityTypes holder, densityfunction package, record-form packets, 9-arg LocalPlayer, abstract Level.fuelValues, 26.3 tag fields) - mechanical repairs, not port defects.
